title: `govulncheck`: known vulnerabilities in the dependency tree

videos.script: Your program is mostly code somebody else wrote. Some of that code has bugs a stranger can use, and when one is fixed, it gets written down. This lesson is about reading that record against your own program. {{database}} The record is the Go vulnerability database. Each entry names a module, the versions that are affected, and the exact functions that were fixed. {{reach}} The tool is govulncheck. It does not stop at your go.mod file. It follows the calls from your main function and asks whether any path reaches one of those functions. Two small programs show the difference. Both import the same package at the same old version. One calls the bad function and fails the check. The other never calls it and passes. {{binary}} Then a built binary, which remembers less than its source, and the reports a pipeline can read. {{fix}} Last, the fixes: a newer module, a newer Go, and a job that runs the check every day, because the database changes even when your code does not.
